evidence_quotes: Tobelo, Indonesia led all hotspots with 11 recorded events — the highest of any single region
Nikolski, Alaska ranked second with 9 events spread across the monitoring window
February 3 was the busiest single day, logging 7 earthquakes — more than double the daily average of ~2.7
Tobelo & Nikolski remain on elevated watch... a larger rupture cannot be ruled out without deeper monitoring data
communities across the Southwest Pacific should maintain tsunami preparedness protocols
criticisms: No concrete 24-hour actions are specified — phrases like 'maintain tsunami preparedness protocols' and 'cannot be ruled out without deeper monitoring data' are not executable directives for a coordinator.

The Risk Watch section does not specify which magnitude bands to watch for in the next 7 days, nor does it define thresholds that would trigger escalation (e.g., 'if another M5.5+ occurs in Tobelo within 48 hours, activate X protocol').

No county, prefecture, or administrative unit is named for resource pre-positioning — 'Tobelo' and 'Nikolski' are place references but no downstream jurisdictions or emergency contacts are identified.
The report lacks any explicit recommendation to contact USGS, PTWC, or local agencies for follow-up — the data caveat mentions these bodies but only to disclaim the report, not to direct action.

Prioritization is partially visible (Tobelo > Nikolski > Iran/Chile) but no explicit 'highest priority' label or tiered action framework is provided, making it hard to allocate limited resources across competing regions.
